sub_palette: japonic backbone + sinitic overlay (intra-family blend, Japonic-leaning)
_note: Intra-East-Asian hybrid (Chinese + Japanese) under the base/hybrid model. BASE_08 (Japonic) x BASE_09 (Sinitic). Both parents are east_asian sub-palettes, so inherits is the SINGLE family east_asian (intra-family blend). A sinicized Sino-Japanese maritime kingdom of the dragon-throne (Ryujin = dragon-god; homeland Ryujo). Backbone = Japonic (phonology, clan structure, the rule/kin/shrine/land register); overlay/substrate = Sinitic (Chinese-model bureaucracy, on'yomi court titles, the tributary system, the river/silk/bureaucratic/material register). civ = feudal. SYNCRETIC religion (honji-suijaku): honors BOTH the Chinese celestial powers (Sinitic names) and the native kami (Japonic names) as one power under two faces. Common-word lexicon is a SINGLE FUSED tongue (Japonic-shaped, Sinitic-substrated; see phonology.fusion_rules); rank titles use the real Sino-Japanese/Ryukyuan register for the *_native forms, English for display. DEITY names draw on BOTH family_east_asian.json theonym sets (Sinitic + Japonic faces), never real gods. [REWORKED 2026-06-28 to base/hybrid model: csv_id HYB_50; all-three alignment; English display titles + native; deep-fusion lexicon + fusion_rules.]

phonology.palette: Japonic base (open CV moras; vowels a i u e o; rendaku) dominant, with a Sino-Japanese (on'yomi) Sinitic substrate: Chinese loanwords read in Japanese phonology, a court/bureaucratic register; clan(-shi) + given.
phonology.phonotactics: strict CV moras, vowel-final (only coda -n); on'yomi compounds in the high register; rendaku in compounds.

sound_changes: Sinitic codas resolved to Japonic CV: -ng>0 with vowel epenthesis, final stops>vowel, tones dropped (only -n survives as a coda)
Sinitic monosyllables read on'yomi and given an open final mora (e.g. jiang>ko/sen, jin>kin, si>shi): vowel-final throughout
Japonic root-initial mora-timing and pitch; rendaku (sequential voicing) in compounds (kawa>-gawa, shima>-jima)
retain Japonic CV-mora shape and the five vowels a i u e o; Sinitic sh/ch/j on'yomi reflexes kept as the high-register seasoning
fusion_rules.source_tilt: river/silk/bureaucratic/material/staple words from Sinitic on'yomi roots (the celestial-bureaucratic substrate of trade and craft: kinu<si, gin<yin, gyoku<yu); rule/kin/shrine/land words from Japonic roots (the ruling clan register: yama, mori, ie, miya); every root then filtered to one Japonic-shaped phonology

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Japonic land/rule/kin/shrine roots + Sinitic river/silk/bureaucratic/material roots, all run through one Japonic-shaped (CV-mora, vowel-final) sound-law; portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. NO slashes - one word per concept.

morphology.patronymic_form: clan/house name (-shi / ujizo) first, then given; Sino-Japanese court titles; -no- linking; on'yomi style-names for officials and clergy.
morphology.compounding_rule: [clan] no [given]; toponyms feature/quality + type, often on'yomi: Dai-jo (great-castle), Ryu-to (dragon-capital), Kin-zan (gold-mountain); rendaku voicing in compounds (kawa -> -gawa).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a sinicized Sino-Japanese kingdom on the Chinese model: the Tei/O over a bureaucracy of court ranks, the dragon-throne; a maritime trading realm)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Sino-Japanese sinicized monarchy, ascending. The Tei (emperor; on'yomi of Chinese 'di') over the O (kings) and Shinno (royal princes); the bureaucracy of Bugyo (commissioner) and Kokushi (province-governor) on the Chinese/Ritsuryo model; the Aji are the local lords (Ryukyuan register); Sakimori guard the frontier. DISPLAY titles are English, save the approved foreign terms Daimyo (duchy) and Shogun (kingdom). The *_native forms are the real Sino-Japanese/Ryukyuan register, for NPC dialogue.
title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, save the approved foreign terms set in 'ruler' (Daimyo for the duchy, Shogun for the kingdom). The *_native conlang forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: clan/house (-shi / ujizo) first, then given; officials take a Sino-Japanese court rank; the cultured a Buddhist or studio name (-in/-an).
people_name_convention.dual_register: the court and bureaucracy use Sino-Japanese (on'yomi) names and titles; the common folk Japanese (kun'yomi) names.
people_name_convention.theophoric: names honor both the kami and the celestial powers + an element: Ryu- (dragon), -maru, Ten- (heaven, on'yomi): e.g. Ryutaro, Tenmaru, names blessing both Terashi-no-kami and Tuli-di.

religion._note: Ryujin is SYNCRETIC (the Sino-Japanese honji-suijaku BELIEF): the world HOLDS each power to be one being under two faces - a Chinese celestial official (Sinitic name) and a native kami (Japonic name). This is a belief, NOT a naming operation: the temple-namer never concatenates the two faces. Each holy site takes ONE name, chosen by its building type (see naming_rule), so naming costs exactly what a single-pantheon culture costs. Across a province the player sees the celestial face on Miao/Jiin halls and the kami face on Miya/Jinja shrines, and infers they are the same power - the syncretism surfaces through the spread of names, not within any one name. Faces draw on BOTH family_east_asian.json theonym sets; never real gods. Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic (all human cultures, per the alignment pass); the dragon-powers of sea and storm are especially honored (Ryujo, the dragon-realm).

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers under both faces - Tentei/Takami-no-kami on high, Tuli-di/Terashi-no-kami the just, Aolan-jun/Hagane-no-kami of the sworn war, Lianta-mu/Megumi-hime the merciful - and wards the Chaotic powers as ma / oni; the celestial rite and the kami-shrine bind alike.
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the ancestral dead (senzo) of the dragon-houses and the local earth-and-grain and sea powers; the great celestial officials and the kami invoked situationally at the Miao-hall and the Jinja-shrine; the dragon-kings of the sea especially honored.
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon under both faces (Maluo/Takebi-no-kami, Wuci/Utsuro-no-kami, Lusan/Kogane-Orochi), and names the Lawful celestial order - and Tentei - as the tyrant-heaven to be defied.

religion.naming_rule: ONE name per holy site, selected by building type: a celestial hall (Miao, Jiin) takes the power's .celestial face; a kami-shrine (Miya, Jinja) takes its .kami face. The namer reads one field and formats '[building] of [face]' - identical cost to any single-pantheon culture. NEVER emit both faces in one name. The honji-suijaku identity (the two faces are one power) is surfaced in lore/dialogue text, not in proper names.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: ONE face per site by building type (see naming_rule): celestial hall -> 'the Jiin of Tuli-di', 'the Miao of Gaidun-di'; kami-shrine -> 'the Miya of Terashi-no-kami', 'the Jinja of Iwane-no-kami'. Both kinds occur across a realm; each name carries a single face.
religion.saints_pattern: deified sages, dragon-kings and ancestral heroes; named with the single face matching their site (celestial hall or kami-shrine).

holy_symbol_motifs.Tuli-di: a sun-disc above a coiled dragon and mirror (celestial face)
holy_symbol_motifs.Terashi-no-kami: a rising sun-disc above a mirror and sword (kami face)
holy_symbol_motifs.the dragon-powers: a sea-dragon encircling a flaming pearl
